definitions.explanation: A heated exchange of words between two or more people who disagree. Emphasizes the verbal nature of the conflict — shouting, accusations, and disagreements expressed through words rather than physical action.

examples.japanese: {二人|ふたり}の{言|い}い{争|あらそ}いが{始|はじ}まった。
examples.english: A quarrel between the two of them started.

examples.japanese: {隣|となり}の{部屋|へや}から{言|い}い{争|あらそ}いの{声|こえ}が{聞|き}こえてきた。
examples.english: I could hear the sound of an argument from the next room.

examples.japanese: くだらない{言|い}い{争|あらそ}いはやめて、{冷静|れいせい}に{話|はな}し{合|あ}おう。
examples.english: Let's stop this pointless argument and talk things over calmly.

notes:
USAGE:
Derived from the verb {言|い}い{争|あらそ}う (to argue, to quarrel). Specifically refers to verbal conflicts. Common verbs used with this noun include する (to have), {始|はじ}まる (to start), and {止|や}める (to stop).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {言|い}い{争|あらそ}いになる (it becomes an argument)
- {言|い}い{争|あらそ}いをする (to have an argument)
- くだらない{言|い}い{争|あらそ}い (a pointless quarrel)
- {激|はげ}しい{言|い}い{争|あらそ}い (a heated argument)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- けんか: fight/quarrel — broader; can include physical fighting
- {口論|こうろん}: verbal argument — more formal synonym
- {口|くち}げんか: bickering — more casual, often between close people
